title: Observability Pulse Orchestrator: adaptive SLO thresholds, trace hooks, and anomaly reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an orchestration layer (Pulse Orchestrator) that ties trace-hook enrichment, metrics/log pipeline schema enforcement, and an adaptive SLO engine to reduce false-positive burn-rate alerts and speed up oncall time-to-detect. This ticket covers the end-to-end design, prototype implementation on one critical route (text-generation v1), and a canary of alert tuning using real traffic + synthetic probes.
background: Our current burn-rate alerts are noisy for spiky routes (inference warmup, caching churn). Oncall spends time chasing transient errors that are not customer-impacting. Post-mortems from recent incidents (INC-2025-02-04 & INC-2025-01-12) highlighted gaps: missing trace-context in metric buckets, mismatched log schemas across SDK versions, and no automated mapping between anomalies and probable root cause (model fallback vs infra).
goals: Reduce noisy burn-rate pages on targeted routes by 50% during pilot
Attach top-3 correlated traces/err-logs to every SLO violation alert
Provide an automatic anomaly reconciliation step that downgrades pages to Slack alerts when confidence is low
success_metrics: Pages per 7-day window for gen.v1 route reduced by >=50%
Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for true SLO violations < 5 minutes
Percentage of SLO alerts with trace links >= 95%
technical_design: 1) Trace hooks: extend ingress SDK to embed route+model metadata tags (route_id, model_variant, kv_cache_hit) and add a lightweight sample-id header for tracing. 2) Metrics/log pipeline: add schema v2 (fields: route_id, model_variant, shard_id, kv_cache_hit, seq_len_bucket) enforced in log-collector stage with reject/repair rules. 3) Adaptive SLO engine: dynamic baseline computed from rolling-window p95/p99 with outlier-resistant median-of-means; burn-rate alert thresholds adjusted by traffic volatility score. 4) Anomaly reconciler: for alerts below a confidence threshold run quick correlation (span-duration, error-type histograms, recent deploys) and annotate alert with reason; if confidence < 0.6, send to non-pager channel and create a low-priority incident ticket.
tradeoffs_decisions: Using SDK-level trace hooks increases client release coordination but gives highest fidelity; alternate was edge-proxy enrichment which is looser and would miss some SDK-internal failures
Adaptive thresholds reduce noise but risk delaying detection of real regressions; mitigation: synthetic probes with hard SLO checks remain as guardrail
Schema enforcement will drop malformed logs at ingestion if unrepairable—short term risk to observability coverage; mitigation: replay queue + repair job
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot): implement trace hooks and schema enforcement for gen.v1 route, wire the adaptive engine to that route only, run synthetic probes in parallel. Phase 2: run pilot for 4 weeks, collect data and adjust thresholds. Phase 3: expand to 3 additional high-traffic routes and enable anomaly reconciler. Final: org-wide opt-in with console toggle for adaptive SLOs.

review_feedback: PM (Lina Morris): Prefers conservative default to avoid missing regressions; requested hard failover to existing burn-rate policy for first 2 weeks
Design (Ruth Delgado): Dashboard needs dedicated card showing 'reconciled vs paged' counts to help oncall calibrate

open_questions: What confidence threshold is acceptable for downgrading a page? (suggested default 0.6)
How to surface repaired/dropped events in Console without spamming users? (suggested: single daily digest + per-route sampling)
Can we piggyback trace sampling header onto existing SDK telemetry without increasing payload size significantly?
risks_mitigation: Risk: SDK adoption lag -> Mitigation: proxy enrichment fallback + feature flag per-customer
Risk: Schema enforcement drops important logs -> Mitigation: repair job + replay queue + alert when rejection > 1%
Risk: Adaptive engine masks slow regressions -> Mitigation: synthetic probes with strict SLOs as golden signals
acceptance_criteria: Pilot deployed on gen.v1 with SDK hooks and schema enforcement enabled
>=95% of SLO alerts include at least one linked trace or log sample
Pilot reduces pager volume for gen.v1 by >=50% vs baseline without increasing missed true incidents in synthetic test cases
qa_notes: Test matrix: a) normal traffic baseline b) cache-churn spike (simulate KV cache misses) c) model fallback storm (simulate slow model variant) d) deployment bump with increased tail latency. For each, confirm reconciliation logic marks only low-confidence anomalies as non-pager and that synthetic probe SLOs still page.
